newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Coffee seen pushing higher, needs momentum.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Coffee seen pushing higher, needs momentum.

text.p: MAY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
London's May robusta coffee contract should challenge the psychological $1,600 mark but needs to muster more momentum to revisit last month's peaks above $1,800 a tonne, analysts said on Friday.
The spot position had been trapped in a series of relatively tight ranges this week, finding it difficult to hold above $1,600.
May scored an intra-day high of $1,610 on Thursday but then edged back to close at $1,580, unchanged on the day.
"It's wandering sideways...but there is no actual dynamic which would say there is a lot of support there," said Susan Rigg, a technical analyst at Chart Analysis.
"You can't really say it's doing anything other than consolidating its good rise so far," she said.
Traders called the London market to open between $15 and $20 above Thursday's close.

May had its crucial upside target at last month's double-top formation, two peaks at $1,820 and $1,825 and was well supported from its January/February trading area at values stretching down to $1,421.
But Rigg said a definitive rally was still needed for the upward trend and support levels to be confirmed.
"On the lack of that, I think it's more likely to come down and look at support again. It's going to have to get through $1,680 to say it really has found support.
"But if see a move through the end-March reaction low at around $1,510 I think it's very capable of coming down and looking at lateral support near $1,450."
